importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation between sub-types — single cabin, double-decker, container-type, and multi-room complex are visually distinct and non-interchangeable. Buyers use the image to identify product type and assess build quality before reading any text; wrong type or poor build impression = immediate skip.

Cabin dimensions, wall panel type (PUF/EPS/sheet), seating capacity, and furnishing level are primary shortlisting criteria. A cabin that does not match the site's headcount, insulation requirement, or space constraint is eliminated before any seller contact.

Construction contractors are price-aggressive and compare listings actively. Price varies substantially with cabin size, panel type, and configuration — a 10×10 ft sheet-clad unit and a 40×10 ft PUF-insulated double-decker are not price-comparable, so price is meaningful only after spec confirmation but is a decisive shortlisting signal within a matched spec tier.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall exists in this category; the market is fragmented across regional fabricators and buyers search by spec and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Buyers evaluate whether the seller is a direct manufacturer (vs trader), whether they offer pan-India delivery and on-site installation, and whether they have a track record with similar project types — post-sale relocation and maintenance support are real differentiators in this category.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Custom-dimensioned or large modular complex orders may be quoted per sq ft, but this is a secondary convention; at the listing level, per piece is universally implied for standard catalogue sizes and no buyer questions it.
importance_ranking.reason: Standard catalogue-size bunk house offices are universally sold per piece; no buyer is confused or misled about price by the absence of a unit label on the listing.
